title: Chest X-ray screening
what: A quick image of your lungs for a routine checkup. The radiation dose is very small.
why: Usually once a year at a checkup, for work, school, or registration at a clinic. It helps find tuberculosis and other lung diseases early.
tell_doctor: If you are pregnant or might be
If you have already had a chest X-ray or CT this year

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: No special prep needed. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Take off necklaces and jewelry from your neck. Tie long hair up.

bring: Your referral, if you were given one
steps: You stand with your chest against the panel and rest your chin on the support
When told, you breathe in and hold your breath for a couple of seconds
feel: Nothing. You do not feel the X-ray
after: You can go back to your day straight away
If something is seen, you may be asked for an X-ray or CT. This is not a diagnosis, just a closer look

faq.q: How often can I have a chest X-ray screening?
faq.a: For screening, usually once a year. If you are ill, your doctor may order it more often.

faq.q: Can I have it during pregnancy?
faq.a: It is usually postponed. If the image is really needed, the doctor decides and shields your belly.
